review.summary:
This attempt fixes the problems the last review rejected and solves T-107. `Scene.add_ground` checks the ground kind against `DIFFICULT_GROUND` (heavy snow, ice, rubble, undergrowth), which lives in rules.py and cites GLOSS.difficult-terrain#7. It then reuses the two mechanisms that already exist. For the whole scene, it sets the single `scene.difficult` switch, the same one the rubble trap in traps.py sets. For an area, it calls `mark_difficult`, whose `area.ground` flag movement already reads to slow only walking movers. There is no second whole-scene flag and no write-only key. Any other ground kind is refused with `OutOfScope` (page 181, the same rule) and leaves the scene unchanged. GMs can still use `mark_difficult` directly for the SRD's "something similar" cases.

The tests check behaviour through `move`. They cover each listed kind over the whole scene, where walking costs double and flying costs normal. They also cover a patch: only its squares cost extra, a flier crosses at normal cost, and the kind name is matched loosely ("Heavy-Snow"). A last test checks that an unknown kind is refused cleanly with no state change. Nothing was hard-coded or out of scope.
